To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the HERMES recoil detector has been successfully installed and commissioned.

we have measured: • DVCS on a polarised proton target, • the asymmetry A1, • on a transversally polarised proton target and, • in the kinematic range of 2 < Q2 < 6 GeV2, 0.02 < xB < 0.1, and 1.5 < W < 2.5 GeV.

we have shown that the HERMES Recoil Detector is a well-functioning detector, that the physics potential of the recoil detection method is very high and that we have started to exploit this potential in the first data taken with the Recoil Detector.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structure of nucleons, their constituents (quarks and gluons) and the interactions between them.
the study of hard exclusive reactions in the framework of Generalised Parton Distribution (GPDs).
the structure of the nucleon and in particular with the spin of its quark content.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proton has an angular momentum of about 1/2, but the quarks carry only 1/3, gluons 0, the sea 0 and orbital angular momentum 1/6.
the spin 1 of the nucleon is not carried by quarks, but is due to gluons.
the spin of the proton is not carried by the quark spin alone.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have demonstrated that the recoil detector works well, that we have demonstrated its potential in the analysis of the DVCS reaction, and that we have demonstrated the potential of hard exclusive processes for GPD studies.
we have shown that it is feasible to use the recoil detector to perform exclusive measurements.
the nucleon is not a simple three-quark system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the spin of the proton is not carried by its quarks.
we have demonstrated that the recoil proton can be detected and that the recoil detector is a valuable instrument for the physics programme at HERMES.
we have a new way to probe the spin of quarks.
